answer: Reviewer Stake & Spot-Check 1) Reviewers deposit a security stake, acting as a relic of good behavior. 2) Each review receives a small, random sample of spot-checks, the mirror reflecting potential issues. 3) If a reviewer's work is flagged repeatedly by the beacon of audits, their stake is partially forfeited. Cost for N identities: $50 N. A reviewer must stake $50 initially. The mechanism fails if a sybil attack is small enough that its reviews are unlikely to be spot-checked.
